title: The Treasure in the Temple
lyrics:
[Verse 1]
Josiah fixed up God’s own house,
The workers swept the floor,
And there they found a long-lost book,
God’s words from long before.

[Chorus]
The scriptures are a treasure true,
God’s words for you and me,
They teach us how to do what’s right,
And happy we will be.

[Verse 2]
They brought the book to the young king,
Who listened right away,
His heart was moved; he cried aloud,
“We’ll do what God’s words say!”

[Chorus]

[Verse 3]
Now close your eyes; God’s words are near,
A treasure for your heart,
The Lord is close beside your bed,
You’ll never be apart.

[Chorus]
mood: Reverent music. A slow, stately sway carries the voice like a page being turned with care, matching the wonder of a long-lost book found in the dust of God's house. The chorus rises full and warm, the way a whole room feels when something precious is read aloud. By the last verse the sway grows slower and lower, settling into a quiet, sheltering hush as if the book is closed and set gently by the bed.
